report_name: Everest Ransomware Hits Rail, AI, and Business Intelligence Firms

threat_actors.name: Everest
threat_actors.description: A ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group conducting a double extortion campaign against diverse industrial and technology sectors. The group claimed responsibility for breaches at Stadler, AKM Enterprises Inc., and Conway Analytics, leaking data from Stadler after a ransom was not paid.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through data theft and system encryption.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Used tools like Mimikatz for credential access as part of their typical TTPs.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: Exfiltrated large volumes of sensitive data from victims as part of a double extortion strategy before deploying ransomware. The group was observed using rclone.exe for this purpose.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Encrypted victim systems as the final stage of their attack to pressure victims into paying a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Used the command 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet' to delete Volume Shadow Copies, preventing easy file recovery from system backups.

malware.name: Everest Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload used by the Everest group to encrypt victim systems and conduct double extortion attacks.

tools.name: rclone
tools.description: A legitimate file synchronization tool abused by the Everest group to exfiltrate large volumes of data from victim networks.

tools.name: Mimikatz
tools.description: Mentioned as a tool typically used by Everest for OS Credential Dumping.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Used to delete Volume Shadow Copies with the command 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet' to inhibit system recovery.

identities.name: Stadler
identities.description: A Swiss rail vehicle manufacturer breached by the Everest ransomware group. The company refused to pay the ransom, resulting in the leak of over 270,000 files.

identities.name: AKM Enterprises Inc.
identities.description: A U.S.-based AI and SaaS company listed as a victim on Everest's dark web leak site on July 31, 2026.

identities.name: Conway Analytics
identities.description: A U.S.-based business intelligence firm listed as a victim on Everest's dark web leak site on July 31, 2026.

infrastructure.name: Everest Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the Everest ransomware group to publish data stolen from victims who refuse to pay the ransom.

indicators.name: Rclone Execution for Data Exfiltration
indicators.pattern:
title: Rclone Execution for Data Exfiltration
id: 2a8b3c1d-e4f5-4a8b-9c1d-e2f3a4b5c6d7
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of rclone.exe, a legitimate tool often abused by ransomware groups to exfiltrate large volumes of data.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/top-10-breaches-of-the-week-4/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-01
tags:
  - attack.t1048
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\rclone.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of rclone.exe, a legitimate file sync tool often abused by ransomware groups like Everest to exfiltrate large volumes of data.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: f8a1b2c3-d4e5-4f6a-7b8c-9d0e1f2a3b4c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware tactic to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/07/top-10-breaches-of-the-week-4/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-01
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the command 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet', which is a hallmark of ransomware attacks used to prevent easy file recovery.
